description: This review catalogues 92 urban water demand datasets and 120 related peer-reviewed publications from the last 45 years, from district-level aggregates to household smart meter series and individual fixture end uses. Anna Di Mauro, Andrea Cominola, Andrea Castelletti and Armando Di Nardo published it in Water on 28 December 2020 (volume 13, 2021). Coverage is worldwide. Each dataset is classified by spatial scale, temporal sampling from seasonal to sub-daily, and accessibility, and the authors compare water with electricity demand datasets to show how few water data are open. Format and access: an open access article with tables for district, household and end use datasets, plus supplementary tables. Licence: CC-BY-4.0; free. Caveats: it stops at 2020 and points to datasets, not hosting them. It helps demand modellers find water consumption data for capacity planning and for energy-water studies. Related catalogue records are the DAIAD Alicante smart meter series and the CaRDS California residential water data set.
